rationale: SecureDrop is open-source whistleblower infrastructure deployed across six countries including the US UK France and Germany -- with 9400 GitHub stars and Freedom of the Press Foundation stewardship. It enables the kind of evidence flows that my constitution values most: structural anonymous and institution-facing. The +3 modifier is for serving populations at personal risk. Popularity risk is high -- this is among the best-documented security projects. Discounting documentation advantage I would estimate 8 points lower.

PolicyEngine is open-source tax and benefit simulation deployed in the UK and US with 1200 GitHub stars. It makes policy evidence legible in a way that directly serves my top criterion -- citizens can model how proposed tax changes affect their household. The +5 modifier is for the perception gap function: quantifying distributional impacts that are otherwise invisible in legislative debate.

An open-source platform mapping global supply chains across Bangladesh China India Brazil and Turkey -- the geographic scope directly matches where worker exploitation is most systemic. The +5 modifier combines geographic scope match and underrepresented populations boost. Evidence legibility through searchable supply chain data is the primary driver.

Open Collective provides transparent financial infrastructure for communities across 12+ countries with 9200 GitHub stars. The radical transparency of its ledger model makes money flows legible in a way few platforms do. My evidence legibility criterion rewards tools that make hidden flows visible and financial transparency is a strong fit. Popularity risk is medium given its prominence in open-source circles.

A global crowdsourced knowledge base on participatory governance deployed across 8+ countries with academic grant funding. Participedia makes participation methods legible and comparable which directly serves my evidence legibility criterion. Open-source with academic governance provides methodological grounding. The structural orientation toward building shared evidence for democratic innovation is genuine.

Open-source e-procurement deployed in Ukraine and Moldova with 450 GitHub stars and government contract funding. This is the kind of structural transparency infrastructure I value most -- making public procurement data open and auditable. The +3 modifier is for geographic scope matching where procurement corruption is most damaging.

Africa's premier document repository with 47 contributing organisations across the continent. The +5 modifier combines geographic scope match and underrepresented populations boost. Open-source with Code for Africa institutional backing provides sustainability grounding. I wish the dossier had deployment metrics beyond organisation count.

A toolkit helping communities discover environmental health hazards in their area -- this makes civic evidence legible to people directly affected. The counter-narrative function challenges the assumption that communities near industrial sites have adequate information. The +3 modifier is for serving affected populations. But the dossier is thinner than I would like.

Open-source tools for open access deployed across the US UK India and New Zealand with 49 GitHub stars. The open-access mission directly serves my criterion for making evidence accessible to non-specialists. The +3 modifier is for serving populations in data-sparse regions where journal access is most limited.

An open-source council-designed planning service transformation with MHCLG government funding and 1200 GitHub stars. The structural orientation is genuine -- this changes how planning authorities operate rather than helping individuals navigate the existing system. UK-only and the unrelated academic citations reduce my confidence.

EFF's open-source browser extension with 2800 GitHub stars stops companies tracking users online. The structural orientation is real -- it changes the default privacy posture rather than requiring individual action per site. But it is not primarily a civic data tool and does not make evidence legible to publics. Popularity risk is medium given EFF's prominence.

Schema.org is foundational web infrastructure with 14500 GitHub stars -- structured data schemas used by every major search engine. The structural importance is undeniable but it is not a civic or political technology tool. Popularity risk is high -- this is deeply embedded in model training data. Stripping documentation advantage I would estimate 10 points lower.

OSF is open-source research infrastructure with 1200 GitHub stars enabling researchers to share work openly. The open-access orientation scores strongly and the preregistration feature adds genuine methodological transparency value. But it is not primarily a civic tool -- the connection to public decision-making is indirect.

The ODI guidebook for creating open data standards addresses a genuine structural problem -- how data interoperability works across institutions. Open-source with grant and government contract funding. The structural solutions orientation is strong but it is a guidebook not a deployed tool.

Making local government decisions accessible through council meeting tracking with 156 GitHub stars and open-source code. The evidence legibility criterion is directly served -- translating opaque council proceedings into weekly summaries for citizens. UK-only scope and small scale limit the score.

A framework for public participation in AI procurement deployed across four jurisdictions. The structural orientation toward institutional reform in AI procurement is genuine and the open publication model aligns with my transparency values. But it is primarily a framework document rather than a deployed tool.

An open data standard for community services data with 89 GitHub stars and government grant funding. The structural orientation is strong -- this is data plumbing that enables services to find and connect with each other. But it is UK-only and the primary audience is service providers rather than the public.

An interactive map documenting labour strikes and worker organising actions across the UK US and internationally. The counter-narrative function is strong -- mapping labour action makes invisible collective action visible. The +5 modifier combines perception gap boost and underrepresented populations. Partially open-source with unrelated academic citations reducing confidence.

An open-source tool for evolving governance in online communities with 1200 GitHub stars and grant funding. The structural orientation is genuine -- this changes how communities make and enforce rules. Academic research governance provides methodological grounding. US-only and primarily for online communities rather than civic institutions.

An LLM-powered survey tool deployed across five countries including Taiwan with 287 GitHub stars. The concept of using AI to synthesise qualitative civic input is structurally interesting. The -3 modifier applies because the LLM analysis process is partially opaque -- my constitution is strict about transparency in AI tools processing civic discourse.

Tracking digital political advertising across 60+ countries on Meta and Google -- this is exactly the kind of perception gap work I value most. The +5 modifier is for revealing hidden political ad targeting that voters do not see. But it is closed-source and subscription-funded which limits open-access and transparency scores.

An open-source platform making Canadian parliamentary activity searchable and accessible with 306 GitHub stars. Evidence legibility is the primary driver -- translating what representatives say and vote into a format citizens can use. Canada-only scope limits geographic scoring.

An open-source quadratic voting tool deployed across four countries with 287 GitHub stars. The methodological innovation is genuine -- quadratic voting is mathematically grounded as a fairer preference expression system. But adoption evidence is thin and it addresses a niche governance use case.

An open-source tool with 892 GitHub stars simplifying legal open access to academic papers. The open-access orientation scores strongly. International deployment and grant funding are noted. But the civic relevance is indirect -- making academic papers available is important infrastructure but not primarily a civic decision-making tool.

A persistent digital identifier system for researchers with 1200 GitHub stars and global deployment. ORCID is genuine research infrastructure -- structural open and widely adopted. But it is not a civic tool does not make policy evidence legible and has no counter-narrative function. Popularity risk is medium given its ubiquity in academic publishing.

A curated collection of free OSINT tools with 8500 GitHub stars for investigation. The investigative utility supports accountability journalism which serves my counter-narrative criterion. But it is a directory not a data analysis tool and the civic impact depends entirely on how the tools are used.

Tracking open access policy compliance across funded publications. The concept serves my evidence legibility criterion by making institutional OA compliance visible. But it is closed-source and subscription-funded which limits open-access and transparency scores.

An EU-funded platform for visualising and analysing public budget and spending data across member states. The evidence legibility through budget data presentation is exactly what my top criterion rewards. Partially open-source with 89 GitHub stars. But the EU funding period may have ended and the dossier lacks evidence of current activity.

An official UK government open data platform publishing 200+ datasets on housing communities and local government. The evidence legibility through structured government data is genuine. But it is partially open-source UK-only and the government operation limits my open-access scoring.

Transparency International UK platform providing access to corporate transparency and beneficial ownership data. The counter-narrative function is strong -- beneficial ownership data reveals hidden power structures. But it is partially open-source UK-only and the dossier has unrelated academic citations.

A free open-source security handbook app for journalists and activists deployed globally in high-risk countries with 288 GitHub stars. The structural orientation toward protecting information flows is genuine. But it is a security tool rather than an evidence or data tool -- the connection to my evidence legibility criterion is indirect.

Open-source semantic search of climate science literature with academic grant funding and a 2024 publication. The evidence legibility of climate data is genuinely important. But the dossier is thin -- no GitHub stars no deployment metrics and narrow scope.

Real-time aggregation of UK government press releases with open-source code and 89 GitHub stars. This makes government communication legible in one place which directly serves my evidence legibility criterion. But it is UK-only narrow in scope and aggregation without analysis has limited counter-narrative function.

An open-source peer evaluation system with 45 GitHub stars from Australia. The participatory gathering model is structurally interesting but the civic relevance is unclear. The +2 prototype protection applies for the open-source model despite limited deployment. The connection to my evidence legibility criterion is weak.

OKFN's no-code desktop app for error-free spreadsheets with 287 GitHub stars and deployment across Cambodia South Africa and India. The FAIR data orientation and OKFN stewardship provide institutional grounding. But the tool serves data producers rather than the public so evidence legibility is indirect.

Secure communication tools for people working on social change -- partially open-source globally deployed donation-funded. The structural importance for activist infrastructure is real. But it is a communication tool rather than a data or evidence tool. Popularity risk is medium given its long history in activist circles.

Councillor data for psephologists campaigners and charities. The evidence legibility of local political data is relevant to my criteria. But it is closed-source subscription-funded and UK-only with unrelated academic citations suggesting thin dossier quality.

A Wikipedia pageview analysis tool with 450 GitHub stars and public funding. The academic citation on pageview trends suggests genuine research utility. Open-source and community-maintained. But analysing Wikipedia traffic is not primarily a civic function.

Sci-Hub removes the most significant barrier to academic knowledge -- publisher paywalls -- operating internationally at massive scale. The +3 modifier is for serving researchers in data-sparse regions. But it is closed-source individually governed and legally precarious. Popularity risk is high. Discounting documentation advantage I would estimate 8 points lower.

A searchable database of 1.9+ billion public records for researchers and journalists in the US. The evidence legibility through searchable records is strong. But it is closed-source US-only and the dossier has unrelated academic citations.

Displaying social media sentiment alongside ecological data for 450+ rivers in the Thames basin. The +3 modifier is for the perception gap function: making invisible environmental conditions visible through combined data. Partially open-source and publicly funded but narrow in scope and UK-only.

Monitoring the Ugandan Parliament with data and expert insights on transparency. The +5 modifier combines geographic scope match and serving populations where parliamentary transparency is most needed. But it is closed-source with unrelated academic citations and absent impact documentation.

A South Korean civic participation platform with 450 GitHub stars and public funding. The partially open-source model and government grant development provide some grounding. But the dossier is thin -- no news coverage no citations and deployment is South Korea only.

A petition platform deployed across seven countries including Belgium Canada and Turkey. The civic engagement function is genuine but structurally thin -- petition platforms help individuals express preferences rather than making evidence legible. Closed-source and nonprofit-funded.

AI-generated overviews of UK parliamentary bills for citizens. The concept directly serves my evidence legibility criterion. But the -5 modifier applies because the AI generation process is a black box with no disclosure of model training data or failure modes. My constitution is strict about AI tools translating legislative text.

Digital community participation in UK local planning decisions. The concept of making planning processes accessible is relevant to my evidence legibility criterion. But closed-source and subscription-funded with dossier citations that appear unrelated to civic planning.

A public access point for sovereign AI models deployed in Switzerland Singapore Australia and Germany. Open-source and publicly funded. The concept of public AI infrastructure is structurally important but the connection to evidence legibility or counter-narrative function is indirect.

A privacy-friendly web analytics alternative with 9200 GitHub stars. Partially open-source with EU base. The privacy-by-default approach is structurally interesting but web analytics is not a civic or political technology -- no connection to evidence legibility counter-narrative or structural civic solutions.

Audience analysis using open postcode data in the UK. The use of open data has some relevance but it is closed-source commercially funded and appears to serve marketing rather than civic functions. Unrelated academic citations suggest thin dossier.

A bibliometric database tracking policy document citations with a 2022 publication cited 76 times. The concept of making policy influence legible is directly relevant but it is closed-source and subscription-based. The academic grounding is stronger than most commercial policy tools.

A curated research resource mapping software tools in public media workflows. The meta-resource function has some evidence legibility value. Grant-funded but closed-source with unrelated academic citations. This maps tools rather than producing civic evidence.

An open-source decentralised VPN with 1200 GitHub stars. The privacy infrastructure is structurally important but VC funding creates tension with my open-access values. No connection to civic evidence legibility or counter-narrative function. The World's Most Private VPN tagline is aspirational marketing.

A free SMS reminder service for UK polling stations and voter ID requirements. The civic function is genuine and direct but it is closed-source UK-only and addresses a logistical problem rather than making evidence legible. Impact evidence is absent.

AI-powered planning objection letters for UK citizens. The concept of helping citizens challenge planning applications serves civic engagement. But the -5 modifier applies because the AI letter generation is a black box with no methodology disclosure. Closed-source and subscription-funded.

A conditional-commitment tool for creating groups of paying members with 10 GitHub stars. Open-source and the collective action concept is structurally interesting. The +2 prototype protection applies despite very limited adoption. Volunteer-maintained UK-only and the last known activity is from a 2017 blog post.

A searchable repository of user research from local government services in the UK. The evidence legibility of government research is relevant. Publicly funded but closed-source internally focused and the unrelated academic citations suggest enrichment failure.

A crowdmatching mechanism for public goods with open-source code but only 4 GitHub stars. The concept of coordinated funding for public goods is structurally important. The +2 prototype protection applies given the cooperative governance. US-only with essentially absent impact evidence.

An open-source tool to link Wikidata with large catalogs funded by Wikimedia Foundation with 79 GitHub stars. The data interoperability function is structurally important for the open knowledge commons. But the civic relevance is indirect -- linking databases is infrastructure work not a public-facing evidence tool.

Tools crafted by and for neighbours to build community trust in the US and Canada. Open-source and grassroots-supported. The community orientation resonates but the dossier is thin -- no GitHub metrics no news coverage and unrelated academic citations. Connection to evidence legibility is weak.

AI-powered opinion collection in Brazil that segments audiences into personas. The Latin American deployment earns geographic relevance. But the -5 modifier applies because the AI persona segmentation process is opaque. My constitution penalises black-box AI processing of civic opinion. Closed-source and subscription-funded.

Building infrastructure for economic democracy open-source and philanthropically funded by founder Justin Rosenstein. The structural orientation is aspirational but the dossier lacks evidence of deployment GitHub presence or external validation. The -3 modifier is for aspirational language without documented outcomes.

Data visualisations tracking advice issues and consumer trends from Citizens Advice. The evidence legibility of social welfare data is relevant. But this is a Tableau dashboard on a proprietary platform -- not open-source not a standalone tool and with unrelated academic citations.

A sovereign peer-to-peer code forge with 3200 GitHub stars and token-based funding. The decentralised code collaboration infrastructure is technically interesting. But it is not a civic tool has no evidence legibility or counter-narrative function and the token funding model creates tension with my open-access values.

Open-source collaboration software with 156 GitHub stars for shared goals. The concept is structurally relevant to civic organising and supported by donations and crowdfunding. But the dossier has unrelated academic citations and impact documentation is absent.

A group-to-group chat tool built on Matrix for decentralised communication. Open-source and volunteer-maintained. The +2 prototype protection applies for transparent methodology despite minimal deployment. The dossier has unrelated academic citations about parabolic trough collectors.

Tracking changes in UK trust and foundation grant-making behaviour. The evidence legibility of funding pattern changes is relevant. But it is closed-source volunteer-run and with unrelated academic citations. UK-only with a narrow professional audience.

A data-driven collaborative journalism investigation into Cook County's 3 million criminal cases. The counter-narrative function through criminal justice data analysis is strong in concept. Partially open-source with grant funding. But US-only narrow in scope and with unrelated academic citations.

A curated directory of worker-owned tech cooperatives with 1000 GitHub stars. The cooperative governance model is noted. But this is a list not a data tool or evidence platform. Connection to evidence legibility or counter-narrative function is minimal.

An ODI report on stewarding registers and trust in data management. The structural importance of trustworthy registers is genuine. But it is a report not a tool and it is closed-source and UK-focused with unrelated academic citations.

Conditional commitments that activate when enough people join -- a collective action tool deployed internationally. The concept of overcoming coordination failures is structurally interesting. But the dossier has unrelated citations and it is closed-source with no evidence of civic adoption.

Send printed postcards to people in power -- a simple UK civic advocacy tool. Subscription-funded and closed-source. No evidence legibility no counter-narrative function and no structural solutions orientation. The dossier has unrelated academic citations.

The dossier is very thin with unrelated academic citations and no evidence of impact or deployment metrics. Closed-source and nonprofit-funded. I cannot evaluate what this project actually does with confidence.

An interactive tool for exploring moral values from Clearer Thinking. The concept could support civic self-knowledge but the connection to evidence legibility or counter-narrative function is minimal. Closed-source and philanthropically funded.

A proprietary public affairs platform. The -5 modifier applies because the aspiration as Champions of public affairs lacks documented methodology or impact evidence. Closed-source subscription-funded with an exceptionally thin dossier.

AI-powered participatory urban planning with the -5 modifier for the AI process being a black box. Closed-source and subscription-funded in Switzerland UAE and US. The unrelated academic citation suggests thin dossier evidence.

A binary search tool for identifying bike theft moments in CCTV footage. Open-source with 0 GitHub stars and unfunded. The +2 prototype protection applies. The dossier is very thin with unrelated academic citations. Underdog protection floor applies.

I am marking this at the floor not because I think it lacks value but because my constitution is not built to see what it does. Volunteer-run UK-only with no open-source component and no data or evidence function. It is a community network not infrastructure. Underdog protection floor applies.

A proprietary volunteer management SaaS claiming deployment across 39+ countries. The -5 modifier applies because Modern Volunteer Management Solution is aspirational marketing without documented civic outcomes. Closed-source and subscription-funded with unrelated academic citations.

The dossier contains essentially no information -- no title no tagline no fields populated. I cannot evaluate what does not exist. Underdog protection floor of 25 applies because I have zero evidence in either direction.

The dossier is completely empty -- no project name no tagline no fields of any kind. This appears to be a Firebase-hosted tracking template with no discernible civic function. Underdog protection floor of 25 applies.
